title: Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a framework that predicts what a change to DNA will do in a specified biological setting before researchers construct and test that change. Its intended outputs include molecular effects, such as changes in gene regulation, and selected measurable phenotypes. Predictions would include calibrated uncertainty so that users can distinguish well-supported estimates from cases where the model lacks sufficient knowledge.

In this proposed scope, the biological setting includes cell type, developmental state, environment and genetic background. The goal extends to unfamiliar settings and combinations of variants, where the effect of several changes may not be captured by adding predictions for each change separately. This is a synthesis of the supplied research goal; the retained source does not provide scientific content establishing the extent of these dependencies.

significance.text: If achieved, reliable prospective prediction would let researchers anticipate how genome changes affect regulation and selected traits before building the variants. This could change how experiments are chosen: researchers could compare candidate changes, identify informative tests and prioritize experiments that resolve the greatest uncertainty. These are conditional consequences of the proposed capability, rather than evidence that it is feasible or imminent.

Potential downstream uses include interpreting disease-associated variants, designing biological systems and evaluating changes relevant to crop traits. Such uses would require separate validation in their intended settings. Accurate prediction of a molecular measurement would not by itself establish an organismal outcome, clinical benefit, agricultural performance or safety.

The revolutionary step would be dependable transfer across biological contexts and interacting changes. A strong score for isolated variants on familiar benchmarks would demonstrate a narrower capability. Even a successful framework would need explicit limits on the outcomes, organisms, variant classes and environments for which its predictions are reliable.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this proposal is generalization: learning relationships between genome changes and biological effects that remain useful when the cell state, environment, genetic background or combination of variants differs from the examples used to develop the model. The framework would need to represent interactions among changes and connect sequence-level information to the particular outcomes being predicted.

As an engineering synthesis, concrete barriers include obtaining sufficiently varied experimental data, defining comparable measurements across settings, separating genuine transfer from overlap with training examples, and evaluating combinations without exhaustively testing every possible genotype and context. Connecting molecular effects to selected phenotypes adds another challenge because success at one measurement level does not establish predictive success at another.

Uncertainty must also remain informative outside familiar settings. A useful system would need to recognize when it cannot support a prediction, rather than produce confident estimates for every input. The supplied material does not establish a demonstrated solution to these barriers or a timetable for overcoming them.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies Avsec et al., “Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome,” with a reported publication date of January 28, 2026 and DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10014-0. It attributes to the PubMed abstract predictions of genomic measurements from sequences up to one million bases and performance on variant-effect benchmarks. These details are retained as reported claims: the review could not verify the article identity, date, DOI, sequence-length capability or benchmark results from the retained document.

The retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access barrier, rather than bibliographic information or an abstract. No publisher full text is supplied. Although the research says that publisher full text could not be opened during an earlier check, the supplied review cannot independently establish that access history. The available artifact therefore supports an access limitation, not an assessment of the reported scientific results. This limitation does not show that those results are false.

Even if the reported sequence-length capability and regulatory variant benchmarks are confirmed, those achievements would have to be interpreted within their measured scope. They would not alone establish general prediction of organismal phenotypes across genetic backgrounds and environments, or reliable prediction of unfamiliar variant combinations. No quantitative benchmark scores are supplied here, and none can be reconstructed from the retained artifact.

The supplied review contains no bounded search results with which to assess developments through its stated November 1, 2026 freshness horizon. Consequently, this record cannot establish the latest state of the field or whether the broader goal remains open today. It also provides no basis for classifying the reported AlphaGenome results as disputed or as a preprint.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: make prospective predictions for independently selected single and combined variants across several cell types, developmental settings, environments and genetic backgrounds. Specify the molecular measurements and selected phenotypes in advance, record predictions and uncertainty before experiments, and include contexts and combinations deliberately excluded from model development.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective variant predictions cover contexts and combinations excluded from development

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: independent laboratories should test the predictions against experimental measurements and strong computational baselines. Before testing, the protocol should define selection and sampling rules, outcome-specific accuracy requirements, uncertainty-calibration criteria and what counts as meaningful improvement. These are proposed requirements for a convincing demonstration, not established community standards; the supplied inputs do not justify numerical thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Independent laboratories validate predictions against predefined criteria and strong baselines

completion_criteria.text: Reproducibility should include enough information about model versions, training-data boundaries, experimental conditions and analysis methods for other groups to repeat the evaluation. Results should report performance separately for familiar and unfamiliar contexts, individual and combined variants, and molecular and phenotypic outcomes, so that aggregate success does not conceal important failures.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible evaluations report performance separately across contexts, variants and outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Practical completion would require an explicit statement of the demonstrated domain, including supported organisms, variant classes, outcomes and contexts, along with conditions requiring further experiments or abstention. Finite tests can establish demonstrated breadth and useful reliability within those boundaries; they cannot prove literal universality. Clinical and agricultural deployment would require additional application-specific evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Prediction boundaries specify when further experiments or abstention are required

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins,” overlaps in connecting genome features to biological function. Its emphasis is experimentally establishing causal functions, whereas BIO-03 emphasizes predicting the effects of changes across settings and combinations. Causal experiments could provide training and evaluation evidence for prediction, but predictive performance would not automatically establish a complete causal explanation. The supplied roster supports this conceptual distinction; no detailed BIO-14 research record is available here.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” has broader cellular scope. BIO-03 could contribute a component that predicts responses to genome changes, while a virtual cell would need to represent additional aspects of cellular behavior. Success at variant-effect prediction would not by itself demonstrate an experimentally predictive virtual cell.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-10, “Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale,” concerns measurement capabilities that could help supply context-specific observations and test predicted effects. BIO-15, “Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body,” concerns carrying out changes in targeted cells. Measurement, prediction and delivery are complementary capabilities with separate completion requirements.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” overlaps where genome changes alter protein sequence and function. It focuses on designing enzymes for specified reactions, while BIO-03 covers a broader range of genome changes and their effects across biological contexts. Neither goal subsumes the other, and all remain separate entries.

brief.title: Predicting what DNA changes will do in different settings
possible: Researchers could predict what a change to DNA, the genetic instructions in cells, would do before making it. Predictions would cover gene activity and selected measurable traits, while indicating how much confidence each estimate deserves.

They could compare changes across cell types, stages of development, environments and differences in the rest of the genome. They could also predict what several changes do together, including effects that cannot be found by adding their separate effects.
why: Researchers could choose experiments more effectively. They could compare candidate changes and prioritize tests that answer the most important questions or resolve the greatest uncertainty.
The capability could help researchers interpret DNA differences linked to disease, design biological systems and evaluate changes relevant to crop traits.

sources.who: Žiga Avsec and colleagues at Google DeepMind
sources.showed: AlphaGenome predicts gene activity and other molecular measurements from DNA. It matched or beat leading models on most tests of the effects of DNA changes.
sources.quote: AlphaGenome matches or exceeds the strongest available external models
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates broad prediction of molecular effects from DNA.
sources.not_established: These results do not establish reliable prediction of whole-organism traits across unfamiliar settings and combinations of changes.

sources.showed: Enformer Celltyping predicted chemical marks associated with gene regulation in cell types excluded from training. It used DNA and measurements of how accessible that DNA was to cellular machinery.
sources.quote: Using DNA and chromatin accessibility data for epigenetic imputation, Enformer Celltyping outperforms current best-in-class approaches and generalises across cell types and biological regions.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates transfer of some molecular predictions to unfamiliar cell types.
sources.not_established: Predicting molecular patterns in unfamiliar cells does not establish accurate prediction of the effects of DNA changes in those cells.

sources.who: André M Ribeiro-dos-Santos and Matthew T Maurano
sources.showed: In this preprint, Enformer predicted experimental measurements less well when DNA segments were reordered or reversed. Further training on engineered DNA reduced prediction errors.
sources.quote: We use these data to fine-tune Enformer, yielding significant reduction in prediction error.
sources.cited_for: Tests on engineered DNA reveal failures that familiar sequences can conceal, and provide data for improvement.
sources.not_established: Improvement after further training does not establish reliable predictions for other unfamiliar changes or biological settings.

sources.who: Alexander Karollus, Thomas Mauermeier and Julien Gagneur
sources.showed: Enformer largely captured the effects of promoters, DNA regions where gene activity begins. Models struggled with enhancers, regulatory regions that can act from farther away.
sources.quote:
The most advanced of these sequence-based models, Enformer, by 
and large, captures causal determinants of human promoters.
sources.cited_for: Success near a gene does not establish that a model correctly captures regulation from distant DNA.
sources.not_established: Reliable prediction of distant regulatory effects remained unresolved in the models tested.

shown: Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome predicts a broad range of molecular measurements and performs strongly on tests of DNA change effects. Murphy and colleagues also demonstrated prediction of regulatory marks in cell types excluded from training.

Tests of Enformer expose remaining gaps. Ribeiro-dos-Santos and Maurano found weaker predictions for rearranged DNA, while Karollus and colleagues found failures in predicting distant regulatory effects.
missing: Predictions made before experiments must succeed across unfamiliar cell states, environments, genetic backgrounds and combinations of changes.
Reliable predictions must extend from molecular measurements to the particular traits researchers want to predict.
Independent laboratories must reproduce success against strong alternatives using criteria agreed before testing.
Confidence estimates must remain useful in unfamiliar settings, and models must recognize when they cannot support a prediction.

milestones.label: Advance predictions succeed in unfamiliar settings and combinations
milestones.explanation: Predictions and confidence estimates would have to precede experiments across settings and combinations excluded from development. This would test whether the model transfers beyond familiar examples.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories confirm accuracy against agreed standards
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to test predictions against measurements and strong alternatives using predefined criteria. This would establish whether the gains are meaningful and confidence estimates are trustworthy.

milestones.label: Repeatable evaluations reveal where predictions succeed and fail
milestones.explanation: Other groups would have to repeat evaluations, with results separated by setting, individual or combined changes, and molecular or trait outcomes. This would keep overall scores from concealing failures.

milestones.label: Clear boundaries identify when predictions need experimental testing
milestones.explanation: The framework would have to specify supported organisms, changes, outcomes and settings, plus when it must withhold predictions or require experiments. This would define where its reliability has been demonstrated.

uncertain: How far can models transfer to unfamiliar settings and interacting DNA changes?
Which outcomes and accuracy thresholds would count as success?
Can confidence estimates reliably identify predictions beyond a model’s knowledge?
